sentences.text: Shri Vivek Singh, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Manish Verma, learned Public Prosecutor for the non-applicant/State  Heard learned counsel for the applicant on the question of admission.
The revision seems to be arguable, therefore, admitted for final hearing.
Record of the Courts below be called for.
Also heard on I.A. No.3369/2019, that is an application for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant.
The applicant has been convicted for offence under Sections 7(1) (3) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 & Rule 50(1) read with Section 16(1) (a) (1) (ii) of the Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was were on bail during trial and they have never misused the liberty so granted to them.
However, subject to final outcome of this revision, jail sentence of the applicant may be ordered to be suspended.

After having perused the impugned judgment and on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case I.A.
No.3369/2019 is allowed.

The substantive jail sentence of applicant is suspended subject to his depositing the fine amount and furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-( Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent
